prose.detail:
Identifying the animals is compulsory on every consignment, and it is compulsory animal by animal. The unit record on each commodity line carries `recordCountEquals` against that line's number of animals, so the line is not finished until it holds exactly as many identification records as animals counted, and each of those records must carry at least one identifier ([[c1]]). Until that is true the 'Animal identification details' row on the hub is not complete, and because the review section is gated on every applicable row being complete ([[c2]]), 'Check and submit' reads 'Cannot start yet' — which is what the captured hub shows. A trader bringing in two hundred salmon has to enter two hundred records before the service will show them their own notification.

DR1 asks for identifiers on every species that has an identifier set, but requires them for submission only when the consignment holds more than one species, and even then only one complete record per species: `requiresAnimalIdentifiersForSubmit` is multiple-species AND some-species-has-identifiers, and `hasMinimumAnimalIdentifiersForSubmit` returns true outright when that is false ([[c3]]). So a consignment of a single species can be submitted with nothing identified. dr1-review-notification-incomplete is that case: one species, two cattle, no identifiers entered, and the Identification details card is not marked incomplete and is not among the five entries in the error summary — the five are additional details, arrival details, transport details, roles and addresses and the contact address. `reviewSpeciesCardErrorState` returns no error at all when identifiers are not required for submit ([[c4]]). DR1 does not forget the gap: it carries it forward to the confirmation page as one of two soft follow-ups, 'complete the animal identifier information in the notification' ([[c5]]).

Stop making a complete set of identification records a precondition of reviewing and submitting. Follow DR1's rule: identifiers are required for submission only where more than one commodity line has a typed identifier set, and then only one complete record per line, not one per animal. The per-animal count rule stays as the definition of the task being finished — it is what the hub status and the identification page's counter are built on — but it stops gating the review page, and the outstanding identifiers become a follow-up on the confirmation instead. Order this after review--incomplete-notification-cannot-be-reviewed, which moves the completeness check off the page gate and onto the POST; this finding decides what that check includes. It also decides which cards can carry the per-card error state that finding builds, so the two should be picked up together.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding DR1 refuse Continue, or mark the Identification details card incomplete, on the review page of a single-species notification with no identifiers entered.

prose.detail:
A person identifying an animal is offered at most four identifier types — passport, tattoo, ear tag and horse name — and which of them appear is decided by four commodity allowlists in [[c1]]. A horse, the commodity DR1 asks for a microchip first of all, is asked for two things: fe-animal-identification-horse is headed 'Horse (0101) — Equus caballus' and offers 'Passport number' and 'Horse name' and nothing else. There is no microchip field on any commodity, and no microchip obligation exists to render one: the six unit-record identifier obligations in [[c2]] are passport, tattoo, ear tag, horse name and the two free-text fallbacks.

DR1 asks for a microchip on the two identifier sets a companion animal or an equine falls into. A horse (commodity code 0101) is asked for Microchip, Passport and Horse name, and a cat, dog, ferret or other live mammal (all commodity code 01061900) is asked for Microchip, Passport and Tattoo — [[c3]]. Microchip is the first field on both panels, so it is the identifier DR1 puts in front of the person first.

Add a microchip identifier to the per-animal record: a new unit-record obligation alongside the existing five in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js, a MICROCHIP_COMMODITIES allowlist holding Horse, Cat and Dog in the stub's picker-name vocabulary, a label in the identification copy block, and the new obligation id added to the unit record's requires.anyOfIds so a microchip on its own satisfies the at-least-one-identifier rule. Adding it also widens the derived union behind specificIdentifierWhitelists, which is what stops a microchip-only commodity falling through to the free-text fallback fields.

Every commodity gets an identification record. Where the commodity is on none of the four identifier allowlists — of the five commodities the frontend offers, that is Fish — the record falls back to two free-text fields, 'Identification details' (hinted 'Any other way this animal is identified, if it has no passport, tattoo or ear tag') and 'Animal description'. fe-animal-identification-fish is that page: a salmon line headed 'Fish (0301) — Salmo salar', with those two boxes and no others, asking a person to say in prose how one fish out of a consignment is told from the next. The fallback obligations apply by the inverse gate at [[c1]], and the person must still enter one record per animal counted before the task can complete.

DR1 asks for identification only where the commodity has a typed identifier set. Ornamental fish carries an empty identifier list ([[c2]]), so it gets no panel, and there is no free-text fallback anywhere in DR1. On a consignment where no commodity has identifiers the page does not exist for that person at all: the identification task row is dropped from the notification overview and a request for the page redirects on to additional details.

Two changes travel together and both are needed for the page to behave as DR1 does. Drop the identificationDetails and description obligations so a commodity with no typed identifier gets no fields, and make the identification page and its hub task row conditional on at least one commodity line having a typed identifier — today the page is always reachable and the unit-record count rule still demands one record per animal. Check what the at-least-one-identifier rule on the unit record means once the fallbacks are gone: a fish line would have no identifier obligation able to satisfy it.

The button behaves like every other Save and continue: it saves whatever is in the open record and moves the person to the next page.

DR1's identification page ends with 'Save and continue', the same words as the rest of its journey, and does the same thing — it captures the open record for any single-animal species and moves on ([[c4]], handled at [[c5]]). The person reads 'Animal identification details' at the top of the first page and 'Additional animal details' at the top of the second. Both are authored as the page's own title — [[c1]] and [[c2]] — and the same string is used for the browser tab, so the word 'animal' is repeated in both places on both pages.

DR1 heads the same two pages 'Identification details' ([[c3]]) and 'Additional details' ([[c4]]). Neither carries the word 'animal', because the caption above each heading already says what the page is about — 'About the consignment' on the first and 'Commodity details' on the second — so the heading only has to name the thing being detailed.

Rename the two page headings to DR1's wording, in English and Welsh. This is the page's own heading only: what the hub calls these two tasks is hub--task-row-labels, which asks for the same two words there and says in as many words that the page headings are compared on their own screens. Do the section captions first or at the same time — service-wide--section-caption adds them, and without a caption above it 'Additional details' is a heading that says less than the one it replaces.

prose.detail:
A person can save a cow with only an ear tag, leave the passport and tattoo boxes empty, and the record counts. That is what fe-animal-identification-saved shows: the saved row reads 'Animal 1 — Ear tag: UK123456789012' with no passport in it, and the page has moved the person on to 'Enter details for Bos taurus 2 of 2' rather than presenting the first animal again. Every identifier field is declared optional and the unit record requires just one of the six to be present ([[c1]]); pressing Save and add another with all boxes empty is the only thing rejected, with the at-least-one-identifier message. Once one record exists per animal counted, the task reports itself complete.

DR1 counts an animal as identified only when every field on its commodity's identifier set holds a value — a cow needs both an ear tag and a passport, a horse needs a microchip, a passport and a horse name ([[c2]]). A partly filled record is stored but does not count: the panel presents the same animal again with the values it already has, the entry counter does not advance, and the identification task never reports complete.

Raise the per-record rule from 'at least one identifier' to 'every identifier in scope for this commodity line'. That means changing the unit record's requires from anyOfIds to a rule over the in-scope identifier obligations, and moving the individual identifier obligations from optional to mandatory so each empty box names itself in the error summary rather than the record failing as a whole. Do this after the commodity identifier sets are correct, because the rule is only as good as the set it ranges over — with tattoo still on cattle it would demand a tattoo for every cow. DR1 shows no error message when a record is incomplete, so the messages are the frontend's to author.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding that DR1's identification task reports complete, or that its entry counter advances to the next animal, after a record is saved with one of its identifier fields left empty.

The button inside the record loop reads 'Save and add another' whatever is left to enter, and three captured states now say so. On a line of one animal the counter reads 'Enter details for Bos taurus 1 of 1' and the button still invites the person to add another. On a line of two with one already saved the counter reads 'Enter details for Bos taurus 2 of 2' — this is the last animal there is — and the button still reads 'Save and add another'. Only when the last record is saved does the wording stop being wrong, and that is because the whole entry block goes: the page then shows the saved records and the sentence 'You have entered details for all 2 Bos taurus animals'. So the words never tell the person what pressing them will do next. The button is rendered with no condition of its own at [[c1]].

DR1 makes the in-panel button say what is actually left to do. Where the species has one animal there is no in-panel button at all and the page's own Save and continue captures the record; where more remain it reads 'Save and add another'; and on the last outstanding animal it reads 'Save and finish' ([[c2]]). The captured DR1 panel is two cattle with both outstanding, which is why it shows 'Save and add another'.

Make the in-card button reflect the records still to enter on that line: no button when the line's number of animals is one, 'Save and finish' when this is the last outstanding record, 'Save and add another' otherwise. The card view model already knows the cap and how many units are saved, so the count is to hand. Leave the page-level buttons alone — they are the journey's own pattern and a separate concern.

Each animal already entered appears as one summary-list row: the key reads 'Animal 1' and the value is every identifier joined into one string — 'Passport: UK123456789, Ear tag: UK123456789012' — with a Remove action on the right. The picture is fe-animal-identification-at-maximum, where two cattle read 'Animal 1 — Ear tag: UK123456789012' and 'Animal 2 — Ear tag: UK210987654321' as two `govuk-summary-list` rows; the page holds no table element at all. DR1 shows the same information as a table. The header names the identifiers the commodity asks for, so a cattle panel heads its columns Animal, Ear tag, Passport; each saved animal is one row, labelled with the species name and its number — 'Syncerus spp. 1' — with its values under the matching columns and a Remove button in the last cell ([[c3]]). A person scanning for a missing ear tag reads down one column.

Replace the summary list with a table whose columns are the identifier fields in scope for that commodity line, one row per saved record, keeping the per-row Remove button. The card view model already resolves the scoped fields and each unit's values, so this is a shape change rather than new data. The template renders the inset and then the cards with nothing between them ([[c1]]).

DR1 puts a block headed 'Selected commodities' between the inset text and the first panel. It is a four-column table — Commodity code, Common name, Number of animals, and a Change link on each row that returns to the commodity search — followed by an 'Add another commodity' link ([[c2]]). The cow identification record offers three fields in this order — Passport number, Tattoo, Ear tag number. Tattoo is there because Cow is on the tattoo allowlist alongside Cat and Dog ([[c1]]), which gates the tattoo obligation at [[c2]].

DR1's cattle panel offers two fields, Ear tag then Passport. Tattoo is not on the cattle set at all — [[c3]] gives commodity code 0102 exactly Ear tag and Passport, and Tattoo appears only under 01061900, the cat/dog/ferret code.

Within the five commodities the frontend offers today that means dropping Horse and leaving Cow, which makes the question disappear from a horses-only consignment. DR1 shows the corrected wording: 'has as its aim the sale of or the transfer of ownership', '(for example a gift).', 'or produce offspring.', 'competitive or training events.' and 'or by-product.' The eleven purposes and their hints live in release-agnostic data, so this is what a DR1 user reads ([[c2]]).

Correct the four hints to DR1's wording: fix the apostrophe and drop the comma in Sale/gift, expand 'e.g.' to 'for example' as GDS style requires, and add the missing full stops to Breeding, Racing and Production. Copy only, one file, no behaviour change. The eleven options, their order and their labels already match, so nothing else on the page moves.

Drop the character rule so hyphens, slashes, spaces and full stops are accepted — the whole point of the field is that it is the user's own reference and the service does not read it. Picking Internal market sends the user to a page of its own, 'Purpose in the internal market', with eleven radios. Save and continue with none of them chosen is accepted: the empty value passes validation, the page saves and the user goes on ([[c1]]). Nothing on the page says the answer is needed and no message is ever shown for a missing purpose. The service does hold the rule, but only later: the obligation model makes the purpose mandatory whenever the reason is internalMarket (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js), so the reason hub row stays incomplete and Check your answers cannot be opened until the purpose is chosen. The user meets a page that accepts an empty answer and a hub that will not let them finish, with nothing joining the two up.

DR1 will not let the reason page be saved with Internal market chosen and no purpose behind it. Save and continue returns the page with 'There is a problem' and one entry, 'Select a purpose in the internal market', and the same message appears in red inside the reveal above the eleven radios, with the reveal left open and the red bar running down its edge. The summary link moves focus to the first radio ([[c2]]). This is the state the captured error screen shows. DR1 carries the rule at the later points too — the hub reads the reason task as complete only when the purpose is present ([[c3]]), and Continue on the review page is refused without it ([[c4]]).

Add the page-level check the frontend is missing, so the user is told at the point of the mistake instead of finding a hub row they cannot clear: reject a submit with Internal market chosen and no purpose, with 'Select a purpose in the internal market' in the summary and against the field. The obligation is already mandatory under Internal market, so this is a validator change on one page and nothing in the model moves. Where the message is shown depends on the reveal change: while purpose is a page of its own the error belongs on that page, and once it moves inline it belongs in the reveal, as DR1 shows it. Do this first — it stands on its own.

FALSIFIED BY: Submitting DR1's reason page with Internal market chosen and no purpose selected and reaching the next screen.

prose.detail:
The frontend asks the main reason on its own page and then, depending on the answer, sends the user on to as many as three further pages, each with its own heading, its own Save and continue and its own return to the hub. Internal market leads to 'Purpose in the internal market'. Transhipment or onward travel leads to 'Destination country'. Transit leads to 'Destination country' and then 'Port of exit', in that order. Temporary admission horses leads to 'Port of exit' and 'Exit date'. Reason and purpose sit in one hub task and the other three sit in a second, conditional task called Exit details ([[c1]]). A user answering for transit therefore visits three pages and crosses two hub tasks to answer one question and its consequences.

DR1 asks all of it on one page. The radio group on 'Main reason for import' carries a conditional reveal under four of its five options ([[c2]]), and the questions appear in place the moment the radio is chosen: Internal market reveals the eleven-option 'Purpose in the internal market' radio group; Transhipment or onward travel reveals a Destination country select; Transit reveals Port of exit and then Destination country, in that order; Temporary admission horses reveals an Exit date picker and then a Port of exit select. Re-entry reveals nothing. One page, one Save and continue, one hub task. Every reveal is present in the rendered page and hidden until its radio is chosen, which is why the captured temporary-admission state carries all six reveal fields in its DOM.

Move the four follow-up questions onto the reason page as govukRadios conditional reveals and retire the four separate pages, in reveal order per reason: purpose under Internal market; destination country under Transhipment; port of exit then destination country under Transit; exit date then port of exit under Temporary admission horses. Both the transit pair and the temporary-admission pair come out in the reverse of the frontend's page order today. One consequence follows: the Exit details hub task disappears, and with it the trap where that task renders as a visible unlinked row under Temporary admission horses because its gate tests only the first of its three pages. DR1 has no equivalent trap because it has no second row to gate, so a reason that opens only exit date and port of exit cannot produce a dead row. That hub change is owned by the hub slice and depends on this one. Answers do not need a separate decision: both sides drop a reveal answer once its reason is no longer chosen, so nothing changes about what survives a flip.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding that DR1 routes away from /reason-for-import to a separate page for any of purpose, destination country, port of exit or exit date, rather than rendering it in the conditional block on the reason page itself.

Answering Yes to 'Does the consignment have a region of origin code?' reveals one text box labelled 'Region of origin code', hinted 'For example, FR-75' and five characters wide. The user types the country prefix, the separator and the region part into that one box, and nothing checks that the prefix matches the country they picked above. DR1 reveals the same question as a prefixed input. A read-only grey prefix box, derived from the country of origin the user has already chosen, sits immediately left of a five-character text box. The label is 'Enter the region of origin code' and the hint is 'Enter up to 5 characters', which now describes only the part the user has to supply. On submit the prototype joins the two with a hyphen ([[c2]]). Picking France shows FR, so the user types 75 and the service records FR-75.

Split the field into a country-derived prefix and a suffix input, using the same country-to-prefix mapping the country list already needs, and change the label and hint to match. The Commercial radio is hinted "A business approved to transport animals — you will choose one from a list" and says nothing about where the transporter may be based ([[c1]]). DR1 asserts the restriction three times over. The Commercial option on the type page is hinted "This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland." ([[c3]]). The port-of-entry search offers seventy-eight ports, and two of them are listed twice. Once the means of transport is Railway or Road Vehicle the transit-countries page joins the journey, and the page refuses an empty answer: submitting with no box ticked returns the page with "Select at least one country the consignment will travel through" ([[c1]], copy at [[c2]]). A consignment moving by road or rail that passes through no third country has nothing true to tick, and the only way past the page is to name a country the animals do not travel through.

DR1 shows the same page under the same rule and never validates it. The POST handler saves whatever list arrived and redirects onward ([[c4]]); there is no error branch for transit countries anywhere in the route file, and the completeness helper is explicit that transit countries are optional and any saved list, including an empty one, is acceptable ([[c5]]). A user who travels through nowhere adds nothing and presses Save and continue.

Make transitedCountries optional while it is in scope: drop the empty-answer error from the page, and change the obligation from mandatory to optional so the hub and the review page stop holding the notification open waiting for an answer. The gate that decides whether the page appears at all does not change — Railway or Road Vehicle, on both sides. Do this with the type-ahead change or after it, since both edit the same page and the two are one visit.

prose.detail:
The transport task reaches the transporter question at `/transporters`, which asks "What type of transporter will move the animals?" with two radios, Commercial and Private, and hints that describe what happens next — "A business approved to transport animals — you will choose one from a list" and "You or another individual moving the animals — you will give their address" ([[c1]]). The answer decides the rest of the task: Commercial goes to `/transporters/select`, a radio list of two records, and Private goes to `/transporters/private`, a blank address form. A user who does not know which sort of record theirs is has to guess before seeing anything, and a user whose transporter is already known to the service still starts by answering a classification question. The three pages are ordered type, then list, then form in the section definition ([[c2]]).

DR1 opens the task on `/transporter`, which is the record itself: a lead paragraph naming who a transporter is, the transporter-authorisation guidance, then a heading "Select a transporter", a Search field hinted "Name, address or approval number", and a table of eight approved transporters with a radio in the first column and Name, Address, Approval number, Type and Status columns ([[c3]]). Both commercial and private transporters sit in one table, distinguished by the Type column, so the type is a property of the record shown rather than a question the user answers. Only under the table is there a secondary "Add a transporter" button, and only that button leads to `/transporter/add` — the commercial-or-private question — which opens with the warning "Before you add this transporter, please ensure you have already searched for it first" ([[c4]]). Each row also carries a View details link into the transporter's full record.

Reverse the order of the task. `/transporters` becomes the list page — search over the transporters the service knows about, one row per record showing its type, with a radio to pick one — and the commercial-or-private question moves behind an "Add a transporter" button as the first step of adding a record that is not on the list. The type question keeps its two options but loses the journey-describing hints, because after the move it no longer describes what happens next. Carry the "Before you add this transporter, please ensure you have already searched for it first" warning onto the moved page: it only makes sense once searching comes first. This is the parent of the rest of the transporter findings — the missing search box, the missing approval status, the inability to add a commercial transporter, and the fact that an added transporter is not kept for reuse all land on the list page this creates.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a route in the frontend that reaches a list of transporters without first answering the type question — or finding that DR1 reaches `/transporter/add` from anywhere other than the Add a transporter button on the list.
